answer: One concrete sybil brake: each account must keep a living island of time-stamped work receipts that only that key can re-sign. A relic bond is posted against the island; if a random audit finds the receipts were cloned or back-dated, the bond burns. Because nadir-root lineage tracing links any aliases that share early funding or identical receipt templates, spinning up N fakes means planting N separate islands and locking N relic bonds that cannot share one nadir root. Cost therefore grows with the herd, not with a single reusable identity.
